 Iowa State is back on the road after an upset win over then No. 24 Oklahoma State on Halloween night. Kyle Konrardy hits the game winner to give Jimmy Rogers is first signature win in his Iowa State tenure. This week the Cyclones head to Waco, Texas to take on the Baylor Bears. See how the Cyclone Fanatic staff thinks this game will go down. 
 Chris Williams (7-1): 
 I fully expect Iowa State to be the more engaged football team in this one. The question is if the Cyclones have enough firepower to win on the road against the much healthier Bears. This is a 10-point spread, but I view it much closer to a toss-up. Baylor got the classic dead-cat bounce last week at UCF. Will they be energized by that or should we expect a letdown? I’ll take the Bears by a hair but Iowa State should have a chance in the 4th quarter. Baylor 27, Iowa State 24 
 Rob Gray (6-2): 
 The Cyclones’ offense has feasted on average to bad defenses, but the Bears are rock solid on that side of the ball — and, as mentioned above, feature one of the most fearsome pass rushes in the nation. So don’t expect anything like last week’s eruption in the win over Oklahoma State. ISU should find some success in the running game thanks to Aiden Flora, but will fall a play or two short on the road.  Baylor 27, Iowa State 21 
 Jake Brend (6-2): 
 It’s not every week that you get a potential let down spot for both teams. Iowa State is coming off of their biggest win of the season, Baylor is coming off of the dead cat bounce. What gives?
 Iowa State has played a far tougher Big 12 schedule but Baylor is clearly talented. The numbers show that. But what’s the gap?
 If Jaylen Raynor plays with the freedom he did against Oklahoma State, I really like ISU’s chances to be in a game late in the 4th quarter. However, I’ll give DJ Lagway and his weapons the edge with a late 4th quarter touchdown. Baylor 35, Iowa State 30 
 Jackson Pence (6-2): 
 What an unexpected win for Iowa State last week. That was such a fun moment for Rogers and that football team. Who quiet frankly needed that in the worst way, and so did the fans. 
 This week brings an entirely new challenge. The Baylor Bears. 
 Baylor has been up and down and somehow has a 5-3 record. I think they got their dead cat bounce out of the way last week with UCF after firing Dave Aranda. The Cyclones have plenty of momentum and are playing for a bowl game next week against Cincinnati. I am worried about the injury bug for this team. But I think they escape Waco with a road win. Iowa State 38, Baylor 31 
 Jacqueline Cordova (6-2): 
 I’m not entirely sure what version of the Cyclones we’re getting this weekend on the road, but I’m awfully curious to find out.
 Baylor is riding the momentum of a coaching change, while Iowa State is trying to prove last week’s madness wasn’t a fluke. The Cyclones are banged up, rough around the edges and still figuring things out themselves. But there’s something about a team that’s been kicked around this much and still refuses to roll over.
 And after watching a freshman like Jamal Polite Jr. in last week’s upset….who’s to say there aren’t a few more surprises?
 I don’t expect pretty football, and I don’t expect anything to come easy. But screw it. I’ll gamble. We ball. Iowa State 24, Baylor 21 
 Derek Duke (7-1): 
 If there’s anything we know about the Big 12 this year, when you come off a huge win, you get brought right back down to earth the following week. And with both teams coming off big wins, who knows what will unfold. 
 This game really boils down to which team doesn’t look hungover on Saturday and shows up. The Bears do have some advantages with DJ Lagway and their defense is one of the better ones in the Big 12. If this one were in Ames, I would feel a little better about Iowa State’s chances, but I say this will come down to the wire. Baylor 28, Iowa State 24
